source.title: Fundamental tradeoffs between memorization and robustness in random features and neural tangent regimes

record.file_problem: The full paper, including appendices, is present. Some mathematical notation and formatting are garbled, but the relevant text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test-error behavior in sample-size sweeps using finite-width RF and NTK models. This is a conceptual test of the more-data version, using linearized regimes and reporting test error as a side result of a study primarily about robustness.
record.gate_note: The paper's principal measurements concern the Sobolev-seminorm of robustness, which is not the claim's test-error measure and is not recorded as a row. The authors explicitly state that test error follows similar multiple-descent patterns and report its behavior as sample size and label noise vary. Exact test-error values are shown only in figures. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly about robustness laws, but its finite-width RF and NTK experiments also plot squared test error against sample size. The authors say test error shows the same multiple-descent pattern, with peaks at the interpolation thresholds (n=k, n=kd for NTK; n=d, n=k for RF) and amplification with label noise. This is a result on V3 and V6 in a linearized-network setting (ridge regression on random features or tangent features), not the original deep-network protocol, hence T3. Evidence is figure-only and qualitative.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The main conclusion is proven memorization–robustness tradeoffs: the Sobolev seminorm is lower-bounded by about √n (infinite-width RF/NTK, finite RF) or √(n/k) (finite NTK), and the bounds are tight for min-norm interpolators. As a side observation, robustness shows multiple descent at interpolation thresholds, matching the test-error curves. This multiple descent is amplified by label noise and attenuated by ridge regularization. The authors explain the n=k singularity theoretically only for finite-width RF.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies memorization–robustness tradeoffs in linearized RF/NTK regimes and uses sample-size sweeps; the test-error multiple-descent result is a side finding, not a reproduction of the original deep-network model-size or epoch-wise experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior varies with sample size and label-noise level; experiments also vary activation, ridge parameter, and RF/NTK regime. The text reports that regularization attenuates or removes multiple descent in robustness, but does not make that claim for test error.

fits_no_version.finding: The Sobolev-seminorm (a non-robustness measure) shows multiple descent in n, with singularities at the interpolation thresholds. Ridge regularization reduces it and removes the peaks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Double/multiple descent also appears in statistical functionals other than test error, such as input-gradient robustness of the interpolator.

record.problems: Test-error outcomes are described qualitatively and presented as figures without numerical values or stated uncertainty. Experiments use 10 datasets per sample count and 15 random hidden-weight realizations in the finite-width setups. The sample-count specifications in the RF experiment description and Figure 2 caption differ.
record.rows_left_out: No test-error results relevant to V3 or V6 were left out. Robustness-only results were excluded because Sobolev-seminorm is not the test-error measure in the claim.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep of test error. The RF experiment sweeps k, but test-error results are reported only against n.
No training-time or epoch sweep; models are closed-form ridge solutions.
Deep, fully trained networks; real data. Only synthetic linear-teacher data on the sphere is used.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
Whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak. Only λ in {0, 1e-5, 1e-4, 1e-3} is compared, and no tuning is done.

missing.what: Effect of ridge λ on test-error multiple descent. Authors write 'Notice the attenuation effect of regularization' beside the test-error curves, and later say increasing λ 'kills the multiple-descent' (stated in the seminorm context). No row records test error at λ>0 against λ=0.

record.verdict_notes: The test-error results are incidental and stated only qualitatively; peak locations are read from figures. Activation-specific peak counts (n=k peak only for tanh/erf) are stated for the seminorm, not explicitly for test error. RF sample ranges are inconsistent between the setup and the captions. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep of test error.
No epoch or training-time sweep of test error.
Tested sample-size sweeps in the reported finite-width RF and NTK regimes; no broader set of model classes or settings.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No unified effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across axes.

The paper reports test-error multiple descent and its amplification with increased label noise. It does not establish that optimally tuned regularization removes multiple descent in test error; its explicit regularization claim concerns robustness.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective number of parameters.
